question: The National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021 (MPI) was released by which of the following?
option_4: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
solution_text:
The correct answer is NITI Aayog.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021 Baseline Report was released by NITI Aayog in November 2021. (बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक — नीति आयोग)

 

• The National MPI is based on the UNDP and Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) methodology, measuring poverty across health, education and standard of living using 12 indicators.

 

• A subsequent 'National MPI: A Progress Review 2023' report showed that about 13.5 crore Indians moved out of multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21.

 

• The Baseline Report used data from the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-4), 2015-16.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The global MPI is jointly published by UNDP and OPHI, while the national MPI for India is prepared and released by NITI Aayog.

 

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission in 2015 and also publishes the SDG India Index.

 

NOTE

 

• World Bank (Option 1): Publishes global poverty estimates (e.g., the international poverty line), not India's national MPI.

 

• Ministry of Finance (Option 2): Publishes the Economic Survey, not the MPI.

 

• Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Option 4): Works on welfare of marginalised sections but is not the body that releases the National MPI.

question: In which year did E Gorter and F Grendel make a breakthrough by examining the surface area of lipids and concluded that the lipid surface surrounding cells must be of two layers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1925.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1925, Dutch scientists Evert Gorter and François Grendel extracted lipids from red blood cell membranes and calculated that the lipid layer covering the cells was about twice the surface area of the cell membrane. (कोशिका झिल्ली की द्विस्तरीय संरचना — गोर्टर व ग्रेंडेल, 1925)

 

• This led them to conclude that the cell membrane consists of a lipid bilayer (two layers of lipid molecules), a foundational discovery in cell biology.

 

• Their work laid the groundwork for later membrane models, culminating in the Fluid Mosaic Model proposed by S.J. Singer and G.L. Nicolson in 1972.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Davson-Danielli model (1935) proposed a 'sandwich' structure with protein layers coating the lipid bilayer, later replaced by the fluid mosaic model.

 

• The fluid mosaic model describes the membrane as a fluid lipid bilayer with proteins embedded and floating within it.

 

NOTE

 

• 1910 (Option 1): No such membrane bilayer breakthrough is attributed to this year.

 

• 1945 (Option 3): Predates the fluid mosaic model refinements but is not the year of Gorter and Grendel's discovery.

 

• 1962 (Option 4): Close to when the unit membrane model (Robertson) was discussed, but not the Gorter-Grendel year.

question: Who among the following advocated the ideology of "oru jati, oru matam, oru daivam manushyanu" (one caste, one religion, one god for humankind)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narayana Guru.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sree Narayana Guru, a social reformer and spiritual leader from Kerala, gave the famous maxim "Oru Jati, Oru Matham, Oru Daivam Manushyanu" (One Caste, One Religion, One God for Mankind). (एक जाति, एक धर्म, एक ईश्वर — श्री नारायण गुरु)

 

• He led the movement against caste discrimination and untouchability among the Ezhava community and broader Kerala society in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

 

• He founded the Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam in 1903 to spread his message of social equality.

 

• He is also known for the Aruvippuram Prathishta (1888), where he consecrated a Shiva idol at Aruvippuram, defying caste restrictions on temple worship.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Narayana Guru's disciple Kumaran Asan was a noted poet who furthered his social reform ideas through literature.

 

• His teachings continue to influence Kerala's social and political landscape and are commemorated through Sree Narayana Jayanti.

 

NOTE

 

• Birsa Munda (Option 1): A tribal leader who led the Munda Rebellion (Ulgulan) against British rule and landlords in Chhotanagpur.

 

• Swami Shradhanand (Option 3): An Arya Samaj leader known for the Shuddhi movement and founding Gurukul Kangri.

 

• Keshub Chunder Sen (Option 4): A Brahmo Samaj leader who later founded the Brahmo Samaj of India and advocated the Age of Consent Act.

question: In November 2022, the Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the naming of Greenfield Airport at Hollongi, Itanagar as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Donyi Polo Airport.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In November 2022, the Union Cabinet approved naming the Greenfield Airport at Hollongi, Itanagar (Arunachal Pradesh) as "Donyi Polo Airport, Itanagar". (डोनी पोलो हवाई अड्डा — होल्लोंगी, ईटानगर)

 

• The name "Donyi Polo" means "Sun and Moon" in the local Arunachali language, reflecting the indigenous faith of the region.

 

• The airport was inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi in November 2022, becoming Arunachal Pradesh's first greenfield airport and its first major airport capable of handling large aircraft.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Donyi-Polo is an indigenous animistic religion followed by several tribes of Arunachal Pradesh, worshipping the Sun (Donyi) and the Moon (Polo).

 

• Arunachal Pradesh's other operational airport prior to this was the smaller Naharlagun/Lilabari-linked airstrip; Donyi Polo Airport significantly boosted regional connectivity.

 

NOTE

 

• Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport (Option 1): This is the airport at Guwahati, Assam, not Itanagar.

 

• East Siang Airport (Option 2): Not the official name given to the Hollongi airport.

 

• Changlang Airport (Option 3): Changlang is a district in Arunachal Pradesh but this is not the name given to the Hollongi Greenfield Airport.

question: According to the 2011 Census of India, which state has the highest population in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the 2011 Census of India, Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India, with a population of about 19.98 crore (nearly 20 crore). (सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या वाला राज्य — उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• Uttar Pradesh alone accounts for roughly 16.5% of India's total population, making it more populous than most countries in the world.

 

• Maharashtra ranks second with around 11.24 crore, followed by Bihar at around 10.4 crore.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sikkim has the lowest population among Indian states as per the 2011 Census, while Lakshadweep has the lowest among Union Territories.

 

• India's total population as per the 2011 Census stood at approximately 121 crore, making it the second most populous country in the world at the time.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 1): Third most populous state, not the highest.

 

• West Bengal (Option 2): Fourth most populous state as per the 2011 Census.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Second most populous state, behind Uttar Pradesh.

question: According to a written reply to the Lok Sabha by Government of India, as on 20 July 2022, approximately ________ unorganised sector workers are registered on the e-Shram portal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 28 crores.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per a written reply to the Lok Sabha by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, as on 20 July 2022, approximately 28 crore unorganised sector workers had registered on the e-Shram portal. (ई-श्रम पोर्टल पंजीकरण — लगभग 28 करोड़)

 

• The e-Shram portal was launched on 26 August 2021 to create a National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW), providing each registered worker a 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN).

 

• It covers workers such as migrant labourers, construction workers, gig and platform workers, domestic workers, street vendors, and agricultural labourers, linking them to social security schemes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The e-Shram portal is managed by the Ministry of Labour and Employment and is intended to be integrated with schemes like the PM Suraksha Bima Yojana for accident insurance cover.

 

• Registration on e-Shram is free and open to workers aged 16 to 59 years in the unorganised sector.

 

NOTE

 

• 27 crores (Option 1): Close to, but not the exact figure cited in the July 2022 written reply.

 

• 26 crores (Option 2): An earlier, lower figure than reported as on 20 July 2022.

 

• 25 crores (Option 4): An even earlier figure, below the count reported as on 20 July 2022.

question: Moplahs, or Muslim peasants, created a powerful anti-zamindar movement in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Moplahs (Mappilas), Muslim peasants of the Malabar region of Kerala, led a powerful anti-landlord (anti-zamindar/janmi) movement, culminating in the Moplah Rebellion of 1921. (मोपला विद्रोह — मालाबार, केरल)

 

• The rebellion arose from long-standing agrarian grievances against Hindu landlords (janmis) and British colonial revenue policies, and it later became intertwined with the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movements.

 

• The movement was marked by attacks on landlords' property and, in places, communal violence, and was eventually suppressed by British forces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Moplah uprisings were not a single event — smaller Moplah revolts against landlordism occurred periodically through the 19th century before the major 1921 outbreak.

 

• Variyamkunnath Kunjahammed Haji was a prominent leader associated with the 1921 Moplah Rebellion.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 1): Not associated with the Moplah movement, which was specific to Malabar.

 

• Bengal (Option 2): Saw its own agrarian movements (e.g., Indigo Revolt, Tebhaga), but not the Moplah uprising.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Home to movements like the Awadh Kisan Sabha, but not the Moplah movement.

question:
Match the animals in column A with the phylum they belong to in column B

Column-A                 Column-B

i. Jelly fish             a. Mollusca

ii. Cray fish             b. Mammal

iii. Whale fish           c. Insect

iv. Devil fish            d. Coelenterate
option_1: i - a, ii - c, iii - b, iv - d
option_2: i - d, ii - a, iii - b, iv - c
option_3: i - a, ii - b, iii - c, iv - d
option_4: i - d, ii - c, iii - b, iv - a
solution_text:
The correct answer is i - d, ii - c, iii - b, iv - a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This question tests common (colloquial) animal names that are misleading about the actual phylum/class the animal belongs to. (भ्रामक सामान्य नाम — वास्तविक जगत/संघ)

 

• Jelly fish is not a true fish; it is a Coelenterate (Cnidarian), matching (i - d).

 

• Cray fish is a crustacean, grouped here with the invertebrate/exoskeleton-bearing animals option, matching (ii - c).

 

• Whale fish, despite the name "fish", is treated here as referring to the whale, a Mammal, matching (iii - b).

 

• Devil fish is a common name for the octopus, which belongs to phylum Mollusca, matching (iv - a).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other misleading common names in biology include starfish (Echinodermata, not a fish), silverfish (an insect), and cuttlefish (Mollusca).

 

• Such 'named after but not actually' animal questions are a recurring theme in SSC general science sections.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-a, ii-c, iii-b, iv-d): Incorrectly assigns Jellyfish to Mollusca (a) and Devil fish to Coelenterate (d); the correct pairing is the reverse.

 

• Option 2 (i-d, ii-a, iii-b, iv-c): Incorrectly assigns Cray fish to Mollusca (a) and Devil fish to option (c); Cray fish and Devil fish are swapped relative to the correct match.

 

• Option 3 (i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d): Incorrectly assigns Jellyfish to Mollusca (a), Cray fish to Mammal (b) and Whale fish to (c); none of these match the intended common-name associations.

question: Which part of the Constitution of India incorporates the Directive Principles of State Policy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part IV.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are incorporated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, covering Articles 36 to 51. (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व — भाग IV)

 

• DPSPs were borrowed from the Irish Constitution and are aimed at establishing a welfare state by directing the government in matters of governance and socio-economic policy.

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, DPSPs are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by courts, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country as per Article 37.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III (Articles 12-35), while Part IV-A (Article 51A) contains the Fundamental Duties, added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976.

 

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called the DPSPs 'novel features' of the Indian Constitution, and Granville Austin described Fundamental Rights and DPSPs together as the 'conscience of the Constitution'.

 

NOTE

 

• Part V (Option 2): Deals with the Union Government (President, Parliament, judiciary at the union level).

 

• Part VI (Option 3): Deals with the State Government (Governor, State Legislature, State judiciary).

 

• Part III (Option 4): Contains the Fundamental Rights, not the Directive Principles.

question: Imadshahi family was known for the foundation of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Berar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Imad Shahi dynasty, founded by Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk, established the independent Berar Sultanate after breaking away from the Bahmani Sultanate around 1490. (इमादशाही वंश — बरार सल्तनत)

 

• The Bahmani Sultanate fragmented into five successor states, collectively known as the Deccan Sultanates: Berar (Imad Shahi), Ahmednagar (Nizam Shahi), Bidar (Barid Shahi), Bijapur (Adil Shahi), and Golconda (Qutb Shahi).

 

• Berar was eventually annexed by the Ahmednagar Sultanate in 1574 and later absorbed by the Mughal Empire.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The five Deccan Sultanates jointly defeated the Vijayanagara Empire at the Battle of Talikota (1565).

 

• Of the five, the Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur and the Qutb Shahi dynasty of Golconda survived the longest, until conquered by Aurangzeb in 1686-87.

 

NOTE

 

• Bidar (Option 2): Founded by the Barid Shahi dynasty, not the Imad Shahis.

 

• Ahmednagar (Option 3): Founded by the Nizam Shahi dynasty under Malik Ahmad.

 

• Golkonda (Option 4): Founded by the Qutb Shahi dynasty under Quli Qutb Mulk.

question: The activity of making a human pyramid and putting efforts to break an earthen pot filled with buttermilk is associated with which festival?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Janmashtami.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dahi Handi tradition — forming a human pyramid to break an earthen pot filled with curd/buttermilk suspended at a height — is celebrated during Krishna Janmashtami. (दही हांडी — जन्माष्टमी)

 

• It re-enacts the childhood pranks of Lord Krishna, who, along with friends, would steal and break pots of butter and curd hung out of children's reach.

 

• The festival is celebrated with particular grandeur in Maharashtra, especially in Mumbai and Pune, where teams called 'Govindas' compete to form human pyramids.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Janmashtami marks the birth of Lord Krishna, the eighth avatar of Vishnu, and is celebrated on the Ashtami of Krishna Paksha in the month of Bhadrapada.

 

• The Maharashtra government has recognised Dahi Handi participants ('Govindas') as an 'adventure sport', providing insurance and other benefits.

 

NOTE

 

• Holi (Option 1): The festival of colours, celebrating the arrival of spring and the victory of good over evil (Holika Dahan).

 

• Dushara (Option 3): Marks the victory of Lord Rama over Ravana / Goddess Durga over Mahishasura; associated with Ravana effigy burning, not Dahi Handi.

 

• Mahashivaratri (Option 4): A festival dedicated to Lord Shiva, marked by fasting and night-long prayer, not the Dahi Handi ritual.

question: Who among the following was the author of 'Indica', an account of India under the reign of the Maurya dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Megasthenes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus I Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra, wrote the famous account 'Indica'. (इंडिका — मेगस्थनीज)

 

• Although the original text of Indica is lost, it survives through fragments quoted by later Greek and Roman writers, and provides valuable information on Mauryan administration, society, and economy.

 

• Megasthenes' account describes the seven-fold division of society, the administration of Pataliputra, and the absence of slavery in India (a claim later disputed).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire around 322 BCE after overthrowing the Nanda dynasty, guided by his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya).

 

• Later Mauryan history is chiefly reconstructed through Ashoka's edicts and inscriptions, in addition to Megasthenes' Indica.

 

NOTE

 

• Strabo (Option 1): A Greek geographer and historian who wrote 'Geographica', which quotes Megasthenes but is not itself Indica.

 

• Pliny (Option 2): Roman author of 'Natural History (Naturalis Historia)', which also references India but is a different work.

 

• Diodorus Siculus (Option 3): A Greek historian who wrote 'Bibliotheca Historica', drawing on Megasthenes' account among other sources.

question: Which is the first integrated steel plant in the public sector in India?
option_1: The Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Limited
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rourkela Steel Plant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rourkela Steel Plant, set up in Rourkela, Odisha, with German collaboration, is regarded as the first integrated steel plant in the public sector in India, with production beginning in 1959. (राउरकेला इस्पात संयंत्र — प्रथम सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र एकीकृत इस्पात संयंत्र)

 

• It was set up during the Second Five-Year Plan period, along with Bhilai Steel Plant (Soviet collaboration) and Durgapur Steel Plant (British collaboration), as part of India's post-independence industrialisation drive.

 

• Rourkela Steel Plant introduced LD (Linz-Donawitz) converter technology for steelmaking for the first time in India.

 

• All three plants — Rourkela, Bhilai and Durgapur — are today managed under the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• SAIL (Steel Authority of India Limited) was formed in 1973 as the holding company for India's major public sector steel plants.

 

• The Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO), set up in Jamshedpur in 1907, was India's first integrated steel plant overall, but in the private sector.

 

NOTE

 

• The Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Limited (Option 1): Located in Bhadravati, Karnataka; it began as a private venture (Mysore Iron and Steel Works) before being nationalised, and predates the post-independence public sector plants but is not classed as India's first public sector integrated plant.

 

• The Salem Steel Plant (Option 3): A special steel (stainless steel) plant in Tamil Nadu, commissioned much later (1982), not an early integrated plant.

 

• Indian Iron and Steel Company (Option 4): Originally a private sector company (based in Burnpur, West Bengal), nationalised in 1972, and hence not the first public sector plant.

question: Kamalini and Nalini Asthana were conferred the Padma Shri in 2022 for which of the following?
option_1: For teaching and propagating Kathak globally
option_2: For taking Indian cuisine to the world
option_3: For disaster relief work in Gujarat
option_4: For specialising in the study of Indian society
solution_text:
The correct answer is For teaching and propagating Kathak globally.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kamalini and Nalini Asthana, twin sisters and disciples of the Lucknow gharana, were conferred the Padma Shri in 2022 for their contribution to teaching and popularising Kathak dance across the world. (कमलिनी और नलिनी अस्थाना — कथक नृत्य)

 

• They are noted for training students internationally and for their decades-long dedication to spreading the classical dance form of Kathak.

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, given for distinguished contribution in various fields including art.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, associated with the Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras gharanas (schools).

 

• The Padma Awards are announced every year on the eve of Republic Day and are conferred by the President of India.

 

NOTE

 

• For taking Indian cuisine to the world (Option 2): Not related to the Asthana sisters, who are dancers, not chefs.

 

• For disaster relief work in Gujarat (Option 3): Not their field of contribution; they are Kathak exponents.

 

• For specialising in the study of Indian society (Option 4): Not applicable; their contribution is in classical dance, not sociology.

question: Net Investment plus Depreciation gives an estimate of which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gross investment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By definition, Gross Investment = Net Investment + Depreciation. (सकल निवेश = शुद्ध निवेश + मूल्यह्रास)

 

• Net investment refers to the addition to the capital stock of an economy after accounting for the wearing out (depreciation) of existing capital.

 

• Depreciation (also called consumption of fixed capital) represents the fall in value of capital assets due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or the passage of time.

 

• Adding depreciation back to net investment restores the total (gross) amount spent on capital formation, i.e., gross investment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similarly, Gross Domestic Product (GDP) = Net Domestic Product (NDP) + Depreciation.

 

• Gross investment includes both replacement investment (to cover depreciation) and net new investment (that expands productive capacity).

 

NOTE

 

• Gross Domestic Product (Option 1): Obtained by adding depreciation to Net Domestic Product, not to net investment.

 

• Personal income (Option 2): A measure of total income received by individuals/households, unrelated to the investment-depreciation relationship.

 

• Private investment (Option 4): Refers to investment undertaken by the private sector specifically, not the general net investment plus depreciation relationship.

question: Who among the following Indian classical tabla players was called 'Abbaji'? He collaborated with American jazz drummer Buddy Rich to create a music album in 1968.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alla Rakha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Alla Rakha, the legendary tabla maestro, was affectionately called 'Abbaji'. (अब्बाजी — उस्ताद अल्ला रक्खा)

 

• In 1968, he collaborated with the American jazz drummer Buddy Rich to create the album 'Rich à la Rakha', a landmark fusion of Indian classical percussion and Western jazz drumming.

 

• Alla Rakha was also a long-time accompanist of sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar and is credited with popularising the tabla on the international stage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alla Rakha's son, Ustad Zakir Hussain, went on to become one of the most celebrated tabla players globally, carrying forward his father's legacy.

 

• Alla Rakha was a recipient of the Padma Shri (1977) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 

NOTE

 

• Taufiq Qureshi (Option 1): A percussionist (younger son of Alla Rakha), known for fusion percussion work, but not the one called 'Abbaji' or the 1968 Buddy Rich collaborator.

 

• Zakir Hussain (Option 2): Alla Rakha's son and world-renowned tabla player, but he is not 'Abbaji' — that title belongs to his father.

 

• Fazal Qureshi (Option 3): Another son of Alla Rakha and a tabla player, but not the one referred to as 'Abbaji'.

question: The first phase of the 'action plan for introduction of the Cheetah in India' witnessed ________ being released in the Kuno National Park of Madhya Pradesh in September 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8 cheetahs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under 'Project Cheetah', the first phase of the action plan saw 8 cheetahs (5 females and 3 males) brought from Namibia and released into Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh, on 17 September 2022. (चीता पुनर्स्थापन परियोजना — कूनो राष्ट्रीय उद्यान, 8 चीते)

 

• The release was done by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on his birthday, marking the reintroduction of the cheetah in India, decades after it was declared extinct in the country in 1952.

 

• This was followed by a second phase in February 2023, when 12 more cheetahs were brought from South Africa to Kuno National Park.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Project Cheetah aims to establish a viable cheetah population in India through translocation from Africa, with Kuno National Park as the primary reintroduction site.

 

• The cheetah is the only large carnivore to have gone extinct in India in historic times, primarily due to hunting and habitat loss.

 

NOTE

 

• 10 cheetahs, 6 cheetahs, 12 cheetahs (Options 1, 2 and 4): The actual number released in the first (September 2022) batch from Namibia was 8, not 10, 6, or 12.

question: The famous physicist Victor Franz Hess is known for the discovery of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is cosmic radiation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Victor Franz Hess, an Austrian-American physicist, discovered cosmic radiation (cosmic rays) through high-altitude balloon experiments in 1912. (ब्रह्मांडीय विकिरण — विक्टर फ्रांज हेस)

 

• He found that ionising radiation increased with altitude, proving that it originated from outer space rather than solely from the Earth's own radioactivity.

 

• For this discovery, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1936, shared with Carl D. Anderson.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cosmic rays are high-energy particles (mostly protons) originating from the Sun, supernovae, and other astrophysical sources outside the solar system.

 

• Hess's work laid the foundation for the field of particle astrophysics.

 

NOTE

 

• Quantum statistics (Option 2): Associated with physicists like Bose, Einstein, Fermi and Dirac (Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac statistics), not Hess.

 

• Expanding universe (Option 3): Associated with Edwin Hubble, who observed the recession of galaxies (Hubble's Law).

 

• Theory of super conductivity (Option 4): Associated with physicists like Heike Kamerlingh Onnes (discovery) and Bardeen, Cooper and Schrieffer (BCS theory).

question: Identify the water harvesting system in Western Himalayas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guls.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guls (and Kuhls) are traditional diversion channel-based irrigation and water harvesting systems found in the Western Himalayan region, such as Jammu and Himachal Pradesh, carrying glacier and stream water to fields via gravity. (गुल्स — पश्चिमी हिमालय जल संग्रहण प्रणाली)

 

• These channels tap water from hill streams (khads/nallahs) at a higher elevation and carry it along the contour to agricultural fields at lower elevations.

 

• Kuhls, a related and closely associated system, are especially prominent in Himachal Pradesh (Kangra Valley) for similar surface-flow irrigation purposes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Khadins are traditional water harvesting structures found in Rajasthan (Jaisalmer), using an earthen embankment to trap rainwater runoff for agriculture.

 

• Johads are small earthen check dams used to capture and conserve rainwater, also traditionally used in Rajasthan.

 

NOTE

 

• Khadins (Option 1): A Rajasthan-based rainwater harvesting structure, not from the Western Himalayas.

 

• Johads (Option 2): Traditional Rajasthani rainwater harvesting check dams, not a Western Himalayan system.

 

• None of these (Option 3): Incorrect, since 'Guls' is indeed the recognised Western Himalayan water harvesting system among the given options.

question: Which of the following states has won the 2022 Santosh Trophy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kerala won the 2021-22 Santosh Trophy (played in 2022) by defeating West Bengal in the final, held in Kerala. (संतोष ट्रॉफी 2022 — केरल)

 

• This victory gave Kerala its seventh Santosh Trophy title.

 

• The Santosh Trophy is the premier national football championship contested between Indian states and government institutions, organised by the All India Football Federation (AIFF).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Santosh Trophy is named after Maharaja Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhary of Santosh (Bengal), who donated the trophy in 1941.

 

• West Bengal is historically the most successful team in the tournament's history, with the highest number of titles overall.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 1): Did not win the 2022 edition.

 

• West Bengal (Option 2): Runner-up in the 2022 final, losing to Kerala.

 

• Goa (Option 3): Did not win the 2022 edition of the Santosh Trophy.

question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding composition of the State Legislative Council?

A. The maximum strength of the Council is fixed at one-third of the total strength of the Assembly.

B. The minimum strength of the Council is fixed at 40.

C. A total of 5/6 of the total number of members of a Legislative Council are indirectly elected and 1/6 members are nominated.

D. The nominations (nominated members) made by the Governor can be challenged in the court.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, B and C only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Article 171 of the Constitution, the composition of a State Legislative Council is fixed such that its maximum strength is one-third of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly, and its minimum strength is 40. (विधान परिषद की संरचना — अनुच्छेद 171)

 

• Statement A is correct: The maximum strength is capped at one-third of the Assembly's total strength.

 

• Statement B is correct: The minimum strength of a Legislative Council is fixed at 40 members.

 

• Statement C is correct: Of the total members, 5/6 are elected indirectly — 1/3 by local bodies (municipalities, district boards etc.), 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, and 1/3 by members of the Legislative Assembly — while the remaining 1/6 are nominated by the Governor from persons with special knowledge or experience.

 

• Statement D is incorrect: Nominations made by the Governor to the Legislative Council (for persons having special knowledge or practical experience) are, as a general constitutional principle, not ordinarily subject to challenge in courts, in the same manner as similar Presidential nominations to the Rajya Sabha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• As of now, only six states — Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh — have a Legislative Council (bicameral legislature).

 

• A Legislative Council can be created or abolished by Parliament under Article 169, on the recommendation of the concerned State Legislative Assembly.

 

NOTE

 

• B, C and D only (Option 1): Wrongly excludes A, which is a correct statement, and wrongly includes D, which is incorrect.

 

• A, B, C and D (Option 3): Wrongly includes D as correct.

 

• A, B and D only (Option 4): Wrongly excludes C, which is a correct statement, and wrongly includes D.

question: In which of the following Sessions of the IOC Executive Board Meeting was Brisbane voted to host the 2032 Olympics and Paralympics?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 138th Session held in Tokyo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Brisbane, Australia, was elected as host of the 2032 Summer Olympics and Paralympics at the 138th Session of the International Olympic Committee (IOC), held in Tokyo, Japan, on 21 July 2021. (ब्रिस्बेन — 2032 ओलंपिक, 138वां IOC सत्र, टोक्यो)

 

• This marks the third time Australia will host the Summer Olympics, after Melbourne (1956) and Sydney (2000), and Brisbane becomes the third Australian city to do so.

 

• The decision followed the IOC's newer 'targeted dialogue' process for selecting hosts, rather than the traditional multi-city competitive bidding process.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021 due to COVID-19) and the 138th IOC Session both took place in Tokyo around the same period in July 2021.

 

• The 2028 Summer Olympics are scheduled to be held in Los Angeles, USA.

 

NOTE

 

• 139th Session held in Beijing (Option 1): The 139th IOC Session was linked to the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics period, not the Brisbane 2032 vote.

 

• 137th Session held in Lausanne (Option 3): An earlier IOC session, not the one that elected Brisbane.

 

• 140th Session held in India (Option 4): India hosted the 141st IOC Session in Mumbai (2023); the 140th Session was not held in India, and neither concerns the Brisbane 2032 decision.

question: When did Henry Cavendish report the measurement of the gravitational constant with the mass and density of the Earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is June 1798.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Henry Cavendish reported his famous experiment — measuring the density of the Earth (and thereby the gravitational constant) using a torsion balance — in a paper read to the Royal Society in June 1798, titled 'Experiments to Determine the Density of the Earth'. (कैवेंडिश प्रयोग — जून 1798)

 

• The experiment used a torsion balance apparatus originally designed by Reverend John Michell, which Cavendish refined and used after Michell's death.

 

• Cavendish calculated the Earth's density to be about 5.48 times that of water, remarkably close to the modern accepted value of about 5.51.

 

• Although Cavendish did not explicitly calculate a value for 'G' (the gravitational constant) as such, his result allowed later scientists to derive G from Newton's law of gravitation — hence the experiment is often called 'weighing the Earth'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Cavendish experiment is considered one of the most important early precision experiments in physics.

 

• Henry Cavendish is also renowned for his earlier discovery of hydrogen ('inflammable air') and for research on the composition of water and air.

 

NOTE

 

• March 1795, April 1796, May 1797 (Options 1, 3 and 4): None of these correspond to the actual date; Cavendish's findings were reported to the Royal Society in June 1798.

question:
Which of the following have been characteristics of Green Revolution?

A. Spurt in crop productivity.

B. Shift away from commercial farming to subsistence farming.

C. Rise in acreage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only A and C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution in India (from the mid-1960s), driven by high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, fertilisers and irrigation, was characterised by a spurt in crop productivity and a rise in the acreage (area sown) under these crops. (हरित क्रांति — उत्पादकता वृद्धि, क्षेत्रफल वृद्धि)

 

• Statement A is correct: Yields of crops like wheat and rice rose sharply due to HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, pesticides and assured irrigation.

 

• Statement C is correct: The area under HYV seeds and irrigated cultivation of wheat and rice expanded significantly.

 

• Statement B is incorrect: The Green Revolution actually caused a shift towards commercial (market-oriented) farming, away from subsistence farming, as farmers began cultivating for the market with purchased inputs and high-value cash crops/cereals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution was pioneered in India largely by agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan, working with HYV wheat seeds developed by Norman Borlaug.

 

• It was most successful in states like Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, but also led to regional disparities and environmental concerns like groundwater depletion.

 

NOTE

 

• All – A, B and C (Option 1): Incorrectly includes B, which is a false characteristic (Green Revolution shifted farming towards commercial, not subsistence, agriculture).

 

• Only B and C (Option 2): Incorrectly includes B and excludes A, a correct characteristic.

 

• Only A and B (Option 4): Incorrectly includes B and excludes C, a correct characteristic.

question: Which of the following awards was received by Pandit Birju Maharaj in 1986?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Vibhushan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Birju Maharaj, the legendary Kathak exponent of the Lucknow (Kalka-Bindadin) gharana, was conferred the Padma Vibhushan in 1986. (पद्म विभूषण — बिरजू महाराज, 1986)

 

• He had earlier received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1964 for his contribution to Kathak dance.

 

• He was also honoured with the Kalidas Samman and later the Tagore Ratna Award (2012), among many other accolades over his career.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Birju Maharaj passed away in January 2022; he was widely regarded as one of the greatest Kathak dancers and choreographers of modern India.

 

• He choreographed dance sequences for several Bollywood films, including 'Devdas' (2002) and 'Bajirao Mastani' (2015).

 

NOTE

 

• Padma Shri (Option 1): A civilian award of a lower tier than what he received in 1986; not the 1986 award.

 

• Sangeet Natak Akademi (Option 2): This award was conferred on him earlier, in 1964, not in 1986.

 

• Padma Bhushan (Option 4): A civilian award tier between Padma Shri and Padma Vibhushan; this was not the award he received in 1986 (he was awarded the higher Padma Vibhushan that year).
